title: Cyclic Induction for ZMod n — Adapt Induction to Cyclic Structures

problemStatement.formal:
\forall n \geq 1,\; \forall P : \mathbb{Z}/n\mathbb{Z} \to \text{Prop},\quad
P(0) \;\wedge\; \bigl(\forall k,\; P(k) \to P(k+1)\bigr) \;\implies\; \forall k,\; P(k)
problemStatement.plain: Standard mathematical induction works for natural numbers: prove P(0), prove P(n) → P(n+1), conclude ∀n, P(n). But ℤ/nℤ is a finite cyclic group — you can keep adding 1 and eventually wrap back to 0. Does an analogous "cyclic induction" principle hold?
whyMatters: Cyclic induction explains why successor-style reasoning still works on finite cyclic types despite wraparound.
The ZMod formulation turns a familiar induction pattern into a reusable modular-arithmetic principle.
The follow-up lemmas connect induction, generation by 1, period-n functions, and finite sums over ZMod n.

proven: The cyclic induction principle for ZMod n is proved from ordinary Nat induction and ZMod.val (Lean: cyclic_induction).
Every element of ZMod n is generated additively by 1 (Lean: zmod_generated_by_one).
The wraparound law k + n = k and the cardinality/cardinality-step facts are verified (Lean: zmod_add_period, cyclic_induction_card, addOrderOf_one_zmod).
Period-n functions are shown to be determined by their values modulo n (Lean: cyclic_period_principle).
Finite-sum symmetry over ZMod n is formalized, including the odd-n zero-sum corollary (Lean: zmod_sum_neg_involution, zmod_sum_odd_eq_zero).
knownResults.goal: Expose the completed cyclic-induction principle for ZMod n and its modular-arithmetic consequences.
